slides.0.title: Industry, market and Diploma essays
slides.0.subtitle: Producer structure, exports and price bands, plus blind-tasting clues and MW-style essay examples
slides.1.title: Exports and markets
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Exports are falling
slides.1.highlights.0.content: 2025 exports were €555 million (-12%) and 1.8 million hl (-9%), less than half of 2020's 3.8 million hl; 2022 was €773 million (Meininger, citing I numeri del vino / UN Comtrade)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Mostly bottled
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Bottled wine is about 90% of export revenue; bulk is only about €33 million
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Main markets (volume)
slides.1.highlights.2.content: The UK first, the USA second, Brazil third and Canada fourth (2025); Malbec was 69.3% of exported varietal volume in 2023 (INV)
slides.1.content: Argentine exports lean on Malbec and a few markets, and both volume and value have shrunk in recent years.
slides.2.title: Price bands and positioning
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Mid-shelf brand Malbec
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Malbec built a global mid-shelf brand with consistent ripe fruit at accessible prices (WSET study material)
slides.2.highlights.1.title: High-altitude icon wines
slides.2.highlights.1.content: High-altitude icon wines aim at critical scores and higher price points
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Producer structure
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Large groups sit alongside family and boutique estates; detailed market shares must be checked in official reports and are not quoted here
slides.2.content: Argentina has a lot of mid-priced Malbec and a little high-altitude icon wine, and the two ends run on different logic.
slides.3.title: Blind-tasting clues and an essay outline
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Tasting clues
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Malbec: violet, black and blue fruit, plush tannin; Uco: fresh, chalky, bright acidity; Luján: structured; Torrontés: rose, geranium, peach; Patagonian Pinot: cool and fresh
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Essay outline: altitude
slides.3.highlights.1.content: 1) Thesis: altitude is Argentina's most important terroir variable; 2) Mechanism: cooling, day-night swing, UV, acidity; 3) Examples: Luján vs Uco vs Cafayate; 4) Risks and limits: frost, heat, water; 5) Conclusion
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Exam reminder
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Discuss both the mechanism and its limits; Patagonia, cool from latitude rather than altitude, is a good counter-example
slides.3.content: An MW-style essay needs a thesis, mechanism, examples, limits and a conclusion.
About what share of Argentina's 2025 export revenue came from bottled wine?
Which was the second-largest market by volume for Argentine exports in 2025?
The USA; the UK was first and Brazil third.
Why is Patagonia a good counter-example in an essay on altitude?
A. Its coolness comes from latitude and wind, not altitude
